hypothesis: Stocks closing near their daily high are overbought within their intraday range. A Williams-%%R style percentile reversal over 5-day decay captures the fade back to fair value.
Stocks with the highest 5-day cumulative returns are overcrowded momentum trades. Decay-smoothed reversal of the 5-day sum captures the institutional unwind.
Returns that are statistically extreme (far from their 20-day mean in standard deviation units) are most likely to revert. Z-score normalization self-adjusts for each stock's own volatility regime.
Price moves accompanied by abnormally high volume represent crowded institutional activity. Weighting returns by relative volume identifies the most overcrowded positions which revert sharply.

When the arithmetic midpoint of high and low exceeds VWAP, buyers dominated intraday but failed to move the volume-weighted price. This persistent imbalance reverses as late-day sellers absorb supply.
A 5-day price change normalized by the 20-day average price level creates a scale-invariant momentum signal. Extreme values revert as positions become consensus and contrarian capital enters.
A day's volume significantly above its 20-day average signals institutional activity completion. Once the large order is filled, price reverts as the temporary supply-demand imbalance resolves.
An intraday high-low range that is abnormally wide relative to its 20-day average indicates a volatility shock. Shock days are followed by volatility mean reversion and price normalization.
A stochastic-style position of close within its 10-day high-low channel captures medium-term overbought and oversold extremes more robustly than single-day range signals.
Overnight gaps that are large relative to realized price volatility (not absolute size) represent the most statistically meaningful dislocations and produce the strongest mean-reversion signals.
The upper candle shadow (high minus max of open/close) represents failed bullish attempts. Persistent upper shadows signal overhead selling pressure and a bearish short-term outlook.
The lower candle shadow (min of open/close minus low) represents rejected bearish attempts and buying support. Large lower shadows signal strong demand at price lows and bullish reversal potential.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.65, rank(ts_decay_linear(ts_min(open, close) - low, 5)), 0), subindustry)
